short: A counter-service format built around speed and throughput.
seoTitle: QSR — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: A QSR, or quick service restaurant, is a counter-service format built around fast preparation, limited menus and high throughput.
definition: A QSR, or quick service restaurant, is a counter-service format built around fast preparation, limited menus and high throughput. Food courts, burger chains and most takeaway-led outlets fall into this category.
bodyHtml:
Why QSR matters

QSR economics live on throughput. With lower average spend, profit comes from serving more people per hour, which makes queue time and ticket time the metrics that matter most.

How QSR works in practice

Keep the menu narrow enough for consistent short ticket times, use tokens or a queue display so customers do not crowd the counter, and measure orders per hour by day-part rather than sales alone.

faq.question: How is a QSR different from a cafe?
faq.answer: QSR optimises for throughput and short dwell time; a cafe monetises longer stays and higher spend per head.

faq.question: What is the key QSR metric?
faq.answer: Orders served per hour during peak, and the ticket time behind it.
